_comment: The braked deterministic NAS loop registry. Each entry is a routine job fired headless on the always-on NAS behind the three brakes (run.mjs). 'enabled' is the committed greenlight (no default-true) AND means CLOCKED: a loop may ship enabled only when something actually fires it -- an enabled-but-unclocked loop reads GREEN while nothing runs, a check that means nothing (DR-0076 s3 / DR-0277). A loop held off carries disabled_why + re_review. ARMING (corrected 2026-08-06 -- this comment previously said 'adding a loop here does NOT arm it' and 'registered by hand', both overtaken): the fleet is ARMED BY RECORD via the committed ARMED-BY-RECORD file (DR-0247), and a clock is registered either through the DSM Task Scheduler UI or root crontab over SSH -- both equal ways (DR-0272). A lane whose safe pace is slower than any clock available may instead ride the already-armed services-sync manifest as a stamp-gated rider (DR-0277); such a lane needs no entry here. 'kind:deterministic' loops run with NO LLM and keep going whether or not Claude/Dispatch is online; 'kind:ai' loops are delegated to the cap-resume/wake gate and are NOT run by this dispatcher. schedule is documentation for the clock entry; the clock owns the cadence. NOTE: run.mjs kills the WHOLE loop tree at timeout_seconds, so for multi-installer loops the cycle-wide ceiling -- not any per-child timeout -- is what actually bounds every child.

loops.name: health-check
loops.description: The 'is the system up' probe (wf20 class). GETs each HEALTH_TARGETS endpoint (n8n /healthz + Ollama by default); exits 0 only when all are healthy. No LLM. Migrated first per the 2026-06-29 research-review.

loops.name: surface-audit
loops.description: The PROACTIVE surface audit (DR-0086). Runs the human-needs rubric (scripts/surface-audit-rubric.json) against every served surface, writes app/src/lib/audit-findings.json (read through onto the in-app Concerns & Solutions board) + the event reel. Observe-only (no commit/merge), no LLM -- catches the endless-scroll/static-tile/unreachable/dead-end class before Darrell has to name it. Ships inert (needs LOOPS_ARMED).

loops.name: scribe-transcribe
loops.description: Drain the Scribe whisper queue (DR-0236): whisper-queue.jsonl -> local whisper-gpu transcript -> optional nas-llm minutes (only when LLM_URL is set). The consumer (infra/nas-scribe/scribe_queue_consumer.py) carries its OWN three brakes (item+time budget, lock, auto-pause kill-switch, proven-to-catch in CI) stacked under this runner's. Local ML only, no vendor LLM. Ships inert (needs LOOPS_ARMED + a DSM entry).

loops.name: services-sync
loops.description: The self-deploy loop (DR-0236): run every enabled idempotent installer in services.json from the fresh repo mirror, so merging a service to main IS its NAS deploy -- install/repair/start with no human hand. First service: scribe. Installers no-op when already done; a failure fails the run loudly (ntfy). Ships inert (needs LOOPS_ARMED + a DSM entry). Cycle-wide timeout bounds ALL installers together (run.mjs kills the tree), so cheap stamp-gated riders are registered first in services.json and cannot be starved by a slow sibling -- the 2026-08-06 ways-review finding.

loops.name: funnel-watchdog
loops.description: Sovereign-Python detect + bounded restore for the public Funnel (DR-0268; born from the 2026-08-03 double-525 outage every app->NAS transport rode down). Shim -> funnel_watchdog.py (the scribe pattern). Conforms to RECORDED-STATE rule 1: on a dark endpoint it re-asserts ONLY the sovereign recorded rows (/mcp, /nas-photos) via 'funnel --bg --set-path' (full DSM binary path, never 'serve', never the n8n root), then at most ONE synopkg restart, re-assert, re-probe. Failures exit red -> reel + ntfy. Needs its own DSM entry (paste-ready delivered).

loops.name: transcript-backfill
loops.description: The optional dedicated-DSM-clock path to the YouTube caption loader (infra/nas-sme-pipeline/load-transcripts.py). Disabled by record: the services.json trickle rider is the live path. See disabled_why for the additive-rate constraint that governs ever arming this.
loops.disabled_why: Redundant SECOND path to the same loader, and unclocked. The LIVE path is the transcript-trickle services.json rider on the already-armed services-sync clock (DR-0247). This registry entry has no DSM/cron entry, so enabled:true read GREEN while nothing fired it -- a check that means nothing (DR-0076 s3), found by the 2026-08-06 ways review. Worse, if it were ever clocked at --max 8 every 6h it would ADD ~64 videos/day (~128-192 HTTP calls) on top of the rider's ~32, putting the pair at or over the measured ~180/day IpBlocked ceiling. Kept as the documented DSM-clock upgrade for the day the rider's measured pace proves too slow; the loader's single-flight lock prevents overlap but NOT additive volume, so arming this REQUIRES lowering the rider's budget in the same change.
